key_insight: SEFD reconstructs SEC filings into layout-faithful, token-efficient training data for long-context financial language models and evaluation.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineers a large, open, low-overlap corpus for pretraining, benchmarking, and building document systems that must handle complex tables, disclosures, and long financial contexts.
method: Rebuilt SEC EDGAR filings into MultiMarkdown while preserving document layout and structure.
Released SEFD-v1 as a 152B-token public snapshot and analyzed a much larger 18.5M-filing archive.
Created two benchmarks: EDGAR-Forecast for post-cutoff numerical forecasting and EDGAR-OCR for table transcription.
evidence_signal: The corpus is reported to have less than 0.1% overlap with Common Crawl-derived data and includes a 152B-token snapshot plus evaluation tasks grounded in filings.
watch_item: Because the dataset is reconstructed from filings, downstream performance may depend on OCR/layout recovery quality and on careful handling of noisy or malformed source documents.
paper_title: The Stanford EDGAR Filings Dataset: Reconstructing U.S. Corporate and Financial Disclosures into Layout-Faithful and Token-Efficient Pretraining Data
